items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: learned from Dickie Wells who was also engaged to play with Benny that the band had made some records for an English arranger named Spike Hughes.

ctx.x: A few days after my return to New York, I was contacted by Benny Carter who was forming an orchestra. Benny had formed some orchestras before this, one of which had played the Savoy and another the Arcadia. I was very happy about the opportunity of working for Benny because he was my favourite arranger and alto player.

Benny said that he would let me know when the band would begin rehearsing so I went to Leonia, New Jersey, to spend a couple of days with Beezie whom I had not seen for four months. She was working and could not meet me when I returned to New York. When I came from Leonia I learned from Dickie Wells who was also engaged to play with Benny that the band had made some records for an English arranger named Spike Hughes. No one knew where to contact me in New Jersey so I missed my first chance to record with Benny…

But I made the other rehearsals. Benny had discovered three musicians who were in New York. The pianist, Teddy Wilson, Frederic 'Keg' Johnson, a trombonist and George Johnson (no relation to Keg) an alto sax player. The rest of the musicians were Charlie 'Big' Green, ex-Henderson Trombonist, Dickie Wells, trombone, Bill Dillard, Lindon (Lincoln) Mills and myself on trumpets, Glyn Paque, alto sax and Johnny Russel, tenor.
